title: Sickle cell, ITP and immunodeficiency
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's blood or immune disorder.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for chronic immune thrombocytopenia.

HPI
The patient is an 86-year-old male who presents today for a scheduled follow-up regarding his chronic immune thrombocytopenia. He reports feeling generally well and denies any recent episodes of easy bruising, petechiae, or spontaneous bleeding. He notes that he has been compliant with his current management plan and has not experienced any significant changes in his activity level or physical endurance. He denies any recent fevers, chills, or signs of infection. He is here primarily for monitoring of his platelet counts and to discuss his stable condition.

Medication List
1. Prednisone 5mg daily
2. Aspirin 81mg daily
3. Multivitamin daily

Vitals
Blood Pressure: 132/78 mmHg
Heart Rate: 74 bpm
Respiratory Rate: 16 breaths/min
Temperature: 98.6 F
SpO2: 97% on room air
Weight: 175 lbs

Recent Labs
Platelet Count: 88,000/uL
Hemoglobin: 13.4 g/dL
White Blood Cell Count: 7.2 x 10^9/uL
eGFR: 62 mL/min/1.73m2

Review of Systems
The patient denies any recent headaches, dizziness, or syncope. He reports no joint pain or muscle aches. He denies any shortness of breath or chest pain. He denies any recent visual disturbances or auditory changes. He denies any changes in bowel or bladder habits.

Social History
The patient is retired and lives at home with his wife. He enjoys gardening and walking in the neighborhood. He denies tobacco use and reports social drinking on weekends only.

Family History
Father had hypertension and a history of heart disease. Mother had type 2 diabetes. No known family history of bleeding disorders.

Exam
The patient is alert and oriented x3. He is in no acute distress. Skin is intact with no visible petechiae or ecchymosis noted on the extremities or trunk. Mucous membranes are moist. No lymphadenopathy is palpated. Heart sounds are regular with no murmurs. Lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally.

Assessment
1. Chronic immune thrombocytopenia. The patient's platelet count remains stable at 88,000/uL. He continues to tolerate his current maintenance regimen well without significant side effects.

Plan
1. Continue current medications as prescribed.
2. Monitor platelet counts every 3 months.
3. Patient instructed to report any significant bruising or bleeding immediately.
4. Follow up in 3 months for repeat labs.

Electronically signed, P. O'Brien, PA-C, 05/14/2026
